summary.plain: UA1 reported six candidate events in which an isolated high-energy electron was accompanied by missing transverse energy, the signature expected when a W boson decays into an electron and an invisible neutrino. CERN announced the discovery of the W boson at a press conference on 25 January 1983.
summary.technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 103-116: isolated high-transverse-energy electrons with missing transverse energy at sqrt(s) = 540 GeV, with the signature of a two-body decay of a particle of mass ~80 GeV/c^2 and read as p-pbar -> W(+/-) + X, W -> e + nu. Six candidate events were presented by C. Rubbia at a CERN seminar on 20 January 1983; the discovery was announced at a CERN press conference on 25 January 1983.

title: Experimental Observation of Isolated Large Transverse Energy Electrons with Associated Missing Energy at sqrt(s)=540 GeV
why_it_matters: CERN announced the discovery of the W boson on 25 January 1983; UA1 read its events as production of the charged W, the Intermediate Vector Boson of the unified theory of weak and electromagnetic interactions.
